summary.en: Serving customers smoothly every day, and staying open when things go wrong.
summary.bs: Glatko uslužiti kupce svaki dan, i ostati otvoren kad stvari krenu naopako.

concepts.youtubeQuery: queue management psychology of waiting lines

en.one: Queue management is about reducing how long customers wait, and how long the wait feels.
en.explain: Real waiting drops with more capacity at peak times, appointments, or self-service. Felt waiting drops when people know how long it will take, are kept busy, and see that the line is fair. An unexplained wait always feels longer.
en.example: A bank branch adds a ticket system with a screen showing the expected wait, plus online appointments. Complaints about waiting fall even though the average wait barely changes.
en.why: Long or unfair-feeling queues are one of the fastest ways to lose customers.
en.mixup: Adding staff isn't the only fix. Shifting demand away from peaks, or making the wait feel shorter, can work just as well.

bs.one: Upravljanje redovima znači smanjiti koliko kupci čekaju, i koliko im se čekanje čini dugim.
bs.explain: Stvarno čekanje pada s više kapaciteta u špicama, terminima ili samoposluživanjem. Osjećaj čekanja pada kad ljudi znaju koliko će trajati, kad su nečim zauzeti i kad vide da je red pravedan. Neobjašnjeno čekanje se uvijek čini dužim.
bs.example: Poslovnica banke uvede sistem s brojevima i ekranom koji pokazuje očekivano čekanje, plus online termine. Žalbe na čekanje padnu, iako se prosječno čekanje jedva promijenilo.
bs.why: Dugi ili nepravedni redovi su jedan od najbržih načina da izgubiš kupce.
bs.mixup: Dodavanje radnika nije jedino rješenje. Pomjeranje potražnje izvan špica ili činjenje da čekanje izgleda kraće mogu jednako dobro raditi.

en.one: An SLA is a written promise about the level of service: how fast, how reliable, how available, and what happens if the promise is broken.
en.explain: It turns vague words like 'quick support' into measurable numbers, like 'reply within 4 working hours' or '99.9% uptime'. It often includes compensation, like a discount, when targets are missed.
en.example: A web hosting company promises 99.9% uptime. When the site is down for 10 hours in one month, the client gets 20% off that month.
en.why: Both sides know exactly what to expect, which prevents arguments and makes suppliers comparable.
en.mixup: 99% uptime sounds great, but it still allows over 7 hours of downtime a month. Read the numbers carefully.

bs.one: SLA (ugovor o nivou usluge) je pisano obećanje o nivou usluge: koliko brzo, koliko pouzdano, koliko dostupno, i šta se dešava ako se obećanje prekrši.
bs.explain: Pretvara nejasne riječi poput 'brza podrška' u mjerljive brojeve, npr. 'odgovor u roku od 4 radna sata' ili '99,9% dostupnosti'. Često uključuje naknadu, npr. popust, kad se ciljevi ne ispune.
bs.example: Firma za web hosting obećava 99,9% dostupnosti. Kad stranica ne radi 10 sati u jednom mjesecu, klijent dobije 20% popusta za taj mjesec.
bs.why: Obje strane tačno znaju šta da očekuju, što sprečava svađe i čini dobavljače uporedivim.
bs.mixup: 99% dostupnosti zvuči odlično, ali i dalje dozvoljava preko 7 sati prekida mjesečno. Pažljivo čitaj brojeve.

en.one: Staff scheduling is planning who works when, so you have enough people at busy times and not too many at quiet times.
en.explain: Start from expected demand by hour and day, then match staff to it while respecting labour law, rest times and people's lives. Publish schedules early and keep them fair.
en.example: A restaurant looks at last year's sales by hour and sees Friday 19–21h is three times busier than Tuesday afternoon. It shifts two waiters from Tuesday to Friday.
en.why: Wages are often the biggest cost in services, and good scheduling both saves money and keeps service quality up.
en.mixup: Cutting staff to the bare minimum backfires. Tired staff and long waits cost more than one extra shift.

bs.one: Raspored rada je planiranje ko radi kada, tako da imaš dovoljno ljudi u gužvi, a ne previše kad je mirno.
bs.explain: Kreni od očekivane potražnje po satu i danu, pa uskladi radnike s tim, poštujući zakon o radu, odmore i živote ljudi. Objavi raspored rano i neka bude pravedan.
bs.example: Restoran pogleda prošlogodišnju prodaju po satima i vidi da je petkom 19–21h tri puta veća gužva nego utorkom popodne. Prebaci dva konobara s utorka na petak.
bs.why: Plate su često najveći trošak u uslugama, a dobar raspored i štedi novac i održava kvalitet usluge.
bs.mixup: Smanjivanje radnika na goli minimum se obije o glavu. Umorni radnici i dugo čekanje koštaju više od jedne dodatne smjene.

concepts.local: isporuka na vrijeme i u punoj količini
concepts.youtubeQuery: OTIF on time in full KPI explained

formula.en: OTIF = Orders on time and complete ÷ All orders × 100%
formula.bs: OTIF = Narudžbe na vrijeme i kompletne ÷ Sve narudžbe × 100%

en.one: OTIF measures the share of orders delivered on time and complete, with the right items and quantities.
en.explain: An order only counts if it is both on time and in full. It's a tough, honest measure of delivery performance, used for your own operations and to judge suppliers.
en.example: Out of 200 orders last month, 180 arrived on time, but 10 of those were missing items. OTIF = 170 ÷ 200 = 85%.
en.why: It shows how reliable you really are from the customer's point of view.
en.mixup: Measuring 'on time' alone can look great while customers keep getting incomplete orders.

bs.one: OTIF mjeri udio narudžbi isporučenih na vrijeme i kompletno, s pravim artiklima i količinama.
bs.explain: Narudžba se računa samo ako je i na vrijeme i u punoj količini. To je strogo, pošteno mjerilo isporuke, koje se koristi za vlastite operacije i za ocjenu dobavljača.
bs.example: Od 200 narudžbi prošlog mjeseca, 180 je stiglo na vrijeme, ali 10 od njih nije bilo kompletno. OTIF = 170 ÷ 200 = 85%.
bs.why: Pokazuje koliko si stvarno pouzdan iz ugla kupca.
bs.mixup: Ako mjeriš samo 'na vrijeme', rezultat može izgledati odlično dok kupci stalno dobijaju nekompletne narudžbe.

concepts.youtubeQuery: business continuity plan small business explained

en.one: A business continuity plan says how you will keep running, or restart fast, after a disruption like a fire, flood, IT outage or losing a key supplier.
en.explain: List the activities you can't stop, what they depend on (people, systems, suppliers, premises) and a backup for each. Keep backups of data off-site, know who to call, and test the plan once a year.
en.example: A small accounting office keeps all files in a cloud system with daily backups. When a pipe floods the office, everyone works from home the next morning.
en.why: Many small businesses that suffer a major disruption without a plan never fully recover.
en.mixup: Insurance isn't a continuity plan. It may pay later, but it won't keep your customers while you're closed.

bs.one: Business continuity plan (plan kontinuiteta poslovanja) kaže kako ćeš nastaviti raditi, ili brzo ponovo pokrenuti posao, nakon prekida kao što su požar, poplava, pad IT sistema ili gubitak ključnog dobavljača.
bs.explain: Nabroji aktivnosti koje ne smiješ zaustaviti, od čega zavise (ljudi, sistemi, dobavljači, prostor) i rezervu za svaku. Čuvaj kopije podataka van firme, znaj koga zvati i testiraj plan jednom godišnje.
bs.example: Mala knjigovodstvena kancelarija drži sve fajlove u cloud sistemu s dnevnim kopijama. Kad pukne cijev i poplavi kancelariju, svi sljedeće jutro rade od kuće.
bs.why: Mnoge male firme koje dožive veliki prekid bez plana se nikad potpuno ne oporave.
bs.mixup: Osiguranje nije plan kontinuiteta. Možda kasnije plati, ali ti neće sačuvati kupce dok si zatvoren.

en.one: Sustainable operations means running the business with less energy, less material and less waste, and treating workers and suppliers fairly.
en.explain: Often it goes hand in hand with lean: less waste usually means lower cost. Typical steps: energy-efficient equipment, less packaging, local suppliers, repair and reuse, and measuring your footprint. Larger EU companies now must report on this, and their suppliers are asked for data too.
en.example: A bakery donates unsold bread to a food bank at closing time and switches to LED lighting. Its energy bill drops by 15% and its local reputation grows.
en.why: Customers, big buyers and banks increasingly ask about it, and it often saves money.
en.mixup: Green claims without real changes ('greenwashing') can backfire and, in the EU, break consumer law.

bs.one: Održive operacije znače voditi firmu s manje energije, manje materijala i manje otpada, i pošteno se odnositi prema radnicima i dobavljačima.
bs.explain: Često ide ruku pod ruku s leanom: manje rasipanja obično znači manji trošak. Tipični koraci: energetski efikasna oprema, manje ambalaže, lokalni dobavljači, popravka i ponovna upotreba, i mjerenje svog otiska. Veće EU firme sada moraju izvještavati o ovome, a i od njihovih dobavljača se traže podaci.
bs.example: Pekara na kraju dana donira neprodati hljeb banci hrane i pređe na LED rasvjetu. Račun za struju padne za 15%, a ugled u kraju raste.
bs.why: Kupci, veliki naručioci i banke sve više pitaju o tome, a često i štedi novac.
bs.mixup: Zelene tvrdnje bez stvarnih promjena ('greenwashing') mogu se obiti o glavu i u EU kršiti zakon o zaštiti potrošača.
